correctness.rationale: Every parameter range is explicit: q>=2, degree d=1,2,3, disjoint coloured terminal successors and a single positive graded restriction plus constants. The nonnegative-halfspace affine dependence proof establishes VC<=q for arbitrary real examples, complemented by q shattered singleton stars. Counts at degree 2 exhaust zero/single/double successor cases and exclude a balanced initial online split. The degree-three construction gives full adaptive depth q+1 with explicit hypotheses and terminal count vectors for every binary path, and concept cardinalities provide universal upper bounds. All named nonstandard steps were reconstructed and independently checked on finite instances by the standalone script; finite checks do not replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The first three finite successor caps form a natural learning-complexity filtration in qualified-counting description logics. The theorem determines exact static and adversarial online complexity for every q>=2 rather than a numerical example: it proves a uniform d=2 plateau and the sharp first separation at d=3, witnessed by an explicit all-q complete tree. The contrast is relevant to understanding when even a single counting restriction introduces adaptive sample complexity beyond VC complexity; it does not claim bounds for unrestricted ALCQ.
